content.text: {"kind":"summary","title":"KEEPER: recursive memory error persistence and auxiliary objectives","claims":[{"claim_id":"c1","text":"Recursive textual memory can carry earlier errors into later updates; self-consistency bias is the persistence of incorrect claims already present in incoming memory.","handles":["e29b67df25e19"],"section":"overview"},{"claim_id":"c2","text":"KEEPER compares four auxiliary objectives on information-content and update-sensitivity axes; reward-related prediction scored highest on task performance among evaluated conditions.","handles":["ee9ac94587a9c","e1de130720b5a"],"section":"overview"}],"abstention":null,"question":null,"proposal":"Proposed, not a finding: seed your memory with a known false claim, feed corrective observations, and check whether it persists, alongside whether valid information is retained.","limitation":"Only the abstract was retained; the error-persistence analysis covers one baseline trajectory, so methods, tables and generality are unavailable."}
